items.source: Nvidia press release 'NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director' (8-K exhibit, sec.gov, 23 Nov); AP via WSLS 23 Nov; Yahoo Finance 'Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia. He has a long road ahead in Washington' (23 Nov 09:10 PST); Investing.com (updated 24 Nov 05:52 ET) for Goldman/Raymond James/Tuesday premarket
items.note: Release text: the board acted 'after a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA'; Jones: 'The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA'; Huang: 'I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment', thanking Kress for leading during 'the brief period of disorder'. The release does not mention the SEC examination or Megaspeed. Trump Truth Social: the government 'has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security'; 'If I thought he did something wrong, I wouldn't be recommending to his board to hire him'. Congress: Cornyn 'No national security risk? Based on what?'; Coons questions the claim; Warren: Huang and Nvidia 'still owe Congress answers'; Reps Mast, Moolenaar, Crawford request testimony citing 'significant national security concerns'; Cotton (WSJ) says Lutnick ignored his China chip warnings. Raymond James: 'Nvidia does not get a do-over' (Strong Buy kept). Rabobank's Every: who is held responsible for export-control circumvention if Huang is pressed in Congress. Investing.com: 'reports said the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its China blacklist' - undated, unverified here. No Bessent statement after the reinstatement surfaced in any fetched page. NVDA overnight 163.92 (02:07 ET), -5% premarket at 05:49 ET (Investing.com; ~157 implied, not printed).

items.note: The release itself carries NO orders/backlog figures and no segment margin guide - those are from the slides/call as relayed by BigGo (Investing.com headline: 'AI orders hit $5.7B, revenue up 50%'); Q1 FY27 guide 14.0-14.6bn (+51-57%), EPS 1.30-1.40. Release lists 'component costs' and 'worldwide component availability' among risk factors; no DRAM/memory cost comment captured (Barclays' Long: memory price increases alone can lift hardware sales). Dell reports Tue 24 Nov after close - not observable; DELL +20.46% to 334.91 Monday. Not a calendar item: the earnings date was already in the calendar group; this is the print's content.

items.name: Fed-speak Mon 23 Nov: NY Fed's Williams ('The Economic Mixdown', Mount Saint Vincent, 16:00 ET) - 'the risk to maximum employment is dialed down, but the risk to achieving price stability is dialed up'; 'it is imperative that we restore inflation to our 2 percent target in a timely manner'; 'there is still work to do to get that done'; inflation ~3.5% this year, 'just above 2 percent next year', 2% 'in 2028'; GDP ~2.75% this year and near that next; unemployment to ~4%; AI buildout risks 'two-sided and roughly balanced'; tariff effects 'largely abated'; 'energy prices remain elevated, and the outlook is highly uncertain'; Dec 9 hike priced ~98%; flash PMIs: composite 54.6 (from 55.9, four-month low), services 54.7 vs 55.6-55.7 consensus, manufacturing 54.5 in line
